scenario: A young shepherd has lost count of his flock and fears one has gone missing on the hillside.
instruction_frame: a request to show the character's reaction to the situation
instruction: Show me how Doran reacts when he comes across a young shepherd who's lost count of his flock and is worried about a missing sheep.
response:
Doran found the boy on the hillside, crouched beside a boulder, frantically counting the sheep again. The shepherd couldn't have been more than fifteen, his face flushed with worry.

"Lost one?" Doran asked, approaching with an easy stride.

The boy nodded miserably. "I've counted three times. There should be twenty-seven, but I only see twenty-six. My master will beat me if I come back short."

Doran rubbed his chin thoughtfully. "I saw a ewe caught in a thornbush down the ravine about an hour ago. White face, black legs?"

The boy's eyes lit up. "Yes! That's one of ours!"

"I could show you," Doran said slowly, "but my time's worth something. Two silver coins and I'll take you right to it."

The boy's face fell. "I don't have any money."

"Then give me that cloak. Good wool, that."

The shepherd hesitated, then pulled off his cloak with shaking hands. Doran took it, draped it over his arm, and pointed vaguely toward the empty hills. "Down that way, past the old oak."

He turned and walked off, the cloak warm against his shoulder, leaving the boy to search alone.
